title: A human's gate decision does not drive the native approval as that human (#236)
symptom: closing a scope gate with a human's relayed decision records the relay but runs no specsync change approve, so the agent records the approval itself under a hard-coded or agent identity
trigger: Configure a human, open a scope gate, close it with --close-gate and that human's relay
expected: Chough runs specsync change approve once with the configured human's SpecSync actor and a note quoting their words, before it records the decision
actual: no SpecSync call is made; the approval is left to the agent, which the permission classifier refused as self-approval when tried directly as 0xLeif
steps: chough checkpoint --close-gate "Scope approval" with that human's relay
impact: Human approvals are recorded under the wrong identity or not at all (GitHub #236)
source: GitHub issue #236; red on 0.5.0 at leif/0.6.0-features-red 82c85c99

notes.text: status: open -> verified. Fixed by plan step 6 (PR #238, f70f5727): closing a driving gate runs specsync change approve or review as the configured human (identity from .chough/local/identity.toml or the user file), refusing an unknown or ambiguous human before anything runs. The approval, close-gate and ship cases passed after the 0.5.0 failure; the agent-run dogfood in a throwaway project was not refused by the classifier. The real check with Leif's relayed decision runs at plan step 14.
